continuity_checks: 'The President' means J. Q. Adams. The great-grandfather John Adams died before Henry's birth, and Henry knew nothing of him except as an idea tied to Quincy.
The boy's age at the school walk is 'six... seven at the utmost.' J. Q. Adams is 'close on eighty.'
The fever's effects on character are the old man's uncertain judgment ('could never make up his mind'), not a settled fact.
The Polk remark is the narrator's speculation ('Probably').
The 1848 collapse was at Mount Vernon Street. The death followed the fall 'on the floor of the House'; keep both without contradiction.
Edward Everett is identified as uncle.

essential: Birth on February 16, 1838 on Beacon Hill, christened Henry Brooks Adams. Keep the 'Israel Cohen' branding analogy in condensed form: he was ticketed through life, safeguards that were valuable in 1738 were less so in 1838, yet he consented to his 'excellent hand.'
1844 as the cut between worlds: the railroad, the Cunard steamers, and the telegraph separated him from 'troglodytic' Boston.
Earliest lessons as color, taste, and discomfort: the yellow floor; scarlet fever and the aunt's baked apple; the suffocating move to Mount Vernon Street.

The fever made him smaller and more delicate, the variation from his brothers' type. Give a shortened list of New England traits: doubt, open questions, horror of ennui, passion for companionship with antipathy to society. Keep 'His brothers were the type; he was the variation.' Keep his claim that whatever was peculiar came from education, not character.
New England resistance, the pleasure of hating, and politics as 'the systematic organization of hatreds.'

Winter/summer and town/country as a double nature. Town is restraint, law, unity; country is liberty and sensual multiplicity. Keep a condensed sense catalogue that includes the smell catalogue and the taste of 'A-B, AB.'

Quincy against Boston. Grandfather J. Q. Adams is known only as kind and called 'the President'; the grandmother is 'the Madam.' Quincy lacks Boston style and comforts. Keep his lifelong prejudice against nineteenth-century style: 'born an eighteenth-century child.' Both grandfathers were equally kind; the bias came from association with seasons and places.

The school-walk episode, in full sequence: the passionate refusal; the mother's disadvantage as a guest; the President descends silently, takes his hand, and walks him nearly a mile. Keep the boy's strategic reasoning that he could escape, then the outcome. His respect came from the grandfather's silence and absence of cant. Keep the joke about President Polk's iniquities. Keep the 'stoniest soil' close.

The intimacy afterward: the library, the caterpillars under the Madam's tumblers, the acorns in her cut-glass bowls. The boy brought up the best peaches to rot for seed. Note the inscribed Nursery Rhymes, which suggest possible self-reproach.
Church pews behind two Presidents and the Irish gardener's remark, 'You'll be thinkin' you'll be President too!'

The Madam as an exotic, 'Louis Seize, like the furniture.' Give a compressed life: London birth, Berlin, the St. Petersburg-to-Paris journey in the Cent Jours, 'four miserable years in the White House.' Keep the boy's 'quarter taint of Maryland blood' and his suspicion that her doubts passed to her descendants. Keep the Abigail objection, briefly.

J. Q. Adams's fall and death on February 21, 1848, with the Lunt funeral and Everett's eulogy. Everett could not speak of the Adams quarrel with State Street, the Hartford Convention, or civil war. The ten-year-old 'priest and politician' concludes that Quincy, as resistance to Boston, must be right. Keep the stock-list counterfactual about State Street and the Suffolk Bank.
optional: The Gargantua-Napoleon-Bismarck bells sentence in para 3 can go, provided 'every one must bear his own universe' survives or is paraphrased.
Details of the Brooks houses in Pearl Street and Medford and the history of the Vassall panels, keeping only the old-house/new-style contrast.
The detailed itinerary of Louisa's diplomatic life: Hague appointment, Nantes, Consulate near the Tower, the Senator and Secretary of State years. Keep a few landmarks.
The cottage 'on the hill' and the Bibles and silver mugs joke; cut both together, since the mugs set up the cottage joke.
Dr. Parkman or P. P. F. Degrand dozing by the armchair (para 26), and 'February brought life and death as a family habit.'
Para 25 on Bunker Hill and Boston's colonial deference to English standards can be reduced to one sentence.
risks: The Madam's biography and the sense catalogues are both long and both stylistically rich. Budget pressure may tempt over-cutting the school-walk reasoning, which must stay intact.

title: QUINCY (1838-1848)

verbatim.purpose: Founding question of the whole book; introduces the card-game metaphor.
verbatim.text: What could become of such a child of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when he should wake up to find himself required to play the game of the twentieth?

verbatim.purpose: Authorial statement of the book's method and its self-irony; completes the game metaphor.
verbatim.text: As it happened, he never got to the point of playing the game at all; he lost himself in the study of it, watching the errors of the players; but this is the only interest in the story, which otherwise has no moral and little incident.

verbatim.purpose: Signature ironic contrast between world-historical change and the infant's sense impression.
verbatim.text: Of all this that was being done to complicate his education, he knew only the color of yellow.

verbatim.purpose: Aphorism that seeds the unity/multiplicity theme of the closing chapters.
verbatim.text: Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.

verbatim.purpose: Characteristic barb about teachers, which later turns ironic when he becomes one.
verbatim.text: the man who pretended they were not, was in his eyes a schoolmaster--that is, a man employed to tell lies to little boys.

verbatim.purpose: First instance of the silence motif that recurs to the final chapter.
verbatim.text: Above all, he had held his tongue.

verbatim.purpose: Adam/Adams wordplay; the child's unquestioned continuity.
verbatim.text: no one suggested at that time a doubt whether a system of society which had lasted since Adam would outlast one Adams more.

verbatim.purpose: Chapter's closing cadence of undecided retrospect.
verbatim.text: Sixty years afterwards he was still unable to make up his mind. Each course had its advantages, but the material advantages, looking back, seemed to lie wholly in State Street.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the aged author calls his younger self 'he,' 'the boy,' or 'Henry Adams.' It moves between the child's limited view and the old man's retrospective irony. It relies on aphorism and paradox, such as 'Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.' Self-deprecation is played as mock-scientific analysis: variation, type, force, stamp. Long periodic sentences end in a dry reversal. Lists build through dashes and semicolons. Exact dates anchor the account. Qualifiers like 'perhaps,' 'probably,' and 'he could never decide' recur. Every episode is measured as a lesson in education that taught little or the wrong thing. Double hyphens are characteristic and must be kept.
